physicalNotes: Radius 0.20804746 Jupiter radii from Bonomo et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..33B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract): 14,873.7 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.03272206 Jupiter masses (Bonomo et al. 2023, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2023A&A...677A..33B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Bonomo et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..33B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BONOMO_ET_AL_2023): P 16.141132 d
sources.shape: Bonomo et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..33B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BONOMO_ET_AL_2023): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.1237 au and stellar radius 0.999 solar radii; Bonomo et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..33B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BONOMO_ET_AL_2023): inclination 88.08 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Bonomo et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..33B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BONOMO_ET_AL_2023): transit mid-time 2457920.44584 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 5 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
